subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should claude-cli live-session cleanup remain unconditional at turn end, or should OpenClaw add a bounded drain or telemetry contract for in-flight CLI-owned background grandchildren?
rationale: The source confirms the reported behavior, but changing it affects orphan prevention, process-tree cleanup, model-visible terminal state, and possibly new reliability config/default surface.

options.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
options.body: Add a narrow contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing forced cleanup to the parent/session.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep unconditional cleanup for now, but snapshot and surface killed grandchildren so the silent failure class becomes observable before lifecycle behavior changes.

options.title: Keep cleanup as contract
options.body: Document Claude CLI Workflow/Bash grandchildren as unsupported across turn boundaries and route users to OpenClaw exec/process or detached task surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
recommendation.body: Add a narrow contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing forced cleanup to the parent/session.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the strongest recent Claude live-session history among the likely owners and is closest to the lifecycle contract being decided.
